The Typst back-end's fixture (M098). It declares two indexes and places
neither, so both print at the end of the document in the order declared. It
declares no `lang:`, so every word the index prints is the English default.

Every page below ends in an explicit page break, so the page each mark sits
on is a fact of this source: page 1 is this page, and each break starts the
next. The suite's manifest states every page number from here and nowhere
else.

## Page 1

The first form indexes a term under its own text: [aardvark]{.index}.

A term marked three times on one page prints one locator for the page:
[apple]{.index}, [apple]{.index} and [apple]{.index}.

The second form indexes a term under other text: [the bee]{.index entry="Bee"}.

The fourth form adds an entry with nothing visible: []{.index entry="Cobalt"}.

A principal and an ordinary mark of one term on one page print one bold
locator: [dahlia]{.index} and [dahlia]{.index mention="principal"}.

A range that opens and closes on one page prints that page alone:
[elm]{.index range="open"} and [elm]{.index range="close"}.

A range that closes on the next page opens here: [fig]{.index range="open"}.

A sort key files a term under other text: [The Hague]{.index sort="Hague"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Page 2

The range opened on page 1 closes here: [fig]{.index range="close"}.

The seventh form marks a principal mention: [gnome]{.index mention="principal"}.

The third form nests a term under a parent: [hive]{.index entry="Bee!Hive"}.

The fifth form points at another entry: [insect]{.index see="Bee"}.

The sixth form points at a related entry: [jam]{.index see-also="apple"}.

A term that starts with a digit files under no letter: [42nd Street]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Page 3

The term marked on page 1 is marked again: [apple]{.index}. So is the term
whose see-also mark gave it no locator: [jam]{.index}.

The tenth form files a term in the second index. Thirteen people are named on
this page, one for each letter from A to M:
[Adams]{.index index="people"}, [Babbage]{.index index="people"},
[Curie]{.index index="people"}, [Darwin]{.index index="people"},
[Euler]{.index index="people"}, [Faraday]{.index index="people"},
[Gauss]{.index index="people"}, [Hopper]{.index index="people"},
[Ibn Sina]{.index index="people"}, [Joule]{.index index="people"},
[Kepler]{.index index="people"}, [Lovelace]{.index index="people"} and
[Maxwell]{.index index="people"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Page 4

Thirteen more people are named here, one for each letter from N to Z, so the
index of people runs past the foot of its first column:
[Noether]{.index index="people"}, [Ohm]{.index index="people"},
[Pascal]{.index index="people"}, [Quetelet]{.index index="people"},
[Ramanujan]{.index index="people"}, [Somerville]{.index index="people"},
[Turing]{.index index="people"}, [Ulam]{.index index="people"},
[Volta]{.index index="people"}, [Watt]{.index index="people"},
[Xenakis]{.index index="people"}, [Young]{.index index="people"} and
[Zuse]{.index index="people"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}
